nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly use a chalk-like medium or treatment, rather than merely showing generic blur, grain, or softened photographic detail?
nodes.criteria: pass: identifiable chalk-like marks or surface behavior are visible, beyond generic grain, blur, or softened photographic detail; fail: the image clearly lacks such chalk-like treatment; unknown: the visible evidence does not distinguish chalk-like treatment from generic filtering.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible evidence of chalk-like medium or treatment. Do not assess whether the image is a drawing or whether the conversion covers the whole scene.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly present its content as a drawing rather than as a photograph with blur or texture overlays?
nodes.criteria: pass: substantial depicted content has clearly drawn or illustrated rendering, not merely softened contours or texture over photographic detail; fail: the content remains clearly photographic without a genuine drawing conversion; unknown: evidence does not reliably distinguish a drawing from filtered photographic detail.
nodes.binding: Assess only drawing-versus-photographic rendering. Do not assess chalk medium; do not treat blur, grain, or softened contours alone as proof of a drawing.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Use only saved support observations. complete: n1 and n2 pass and their evidence establishes a chalk-like drawing conversion across the image, not merely a chalk-like surface treatment or isolated sketch-like cues. partial: at least one support provides affirmative evidence of requested transformation, but complete conversion is not established. absent: both supports fail with evidence affirmatively establishing no requested transformation. unknown: evidence is insufficient to determine whether any requested transformation progressed; a failed or unknown cue alone does not establish absence. Do not infer visual facts beyond the supports; unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

Preserve that distinction, but make the complete criterion require affirmative support for both chalk medium and drawing conversion across the image; do not let n1’s chalk-like texture plus n2’s merely sketch-like cues automatically establish a full conversion. Conversely, treat retained photographic detail as evidence against complete conversion, not proof that no requested change occurred: n1’s dusty texture and smudged/sketchy marks are affirmative partial progress. Keep absent reserved for both supports affirmatively showing no progress, and unknown for insufficient evidence. The edited image visibly has a chalky, smudged treatment and softened outlines, while the giraffes and scene remain recognizable and substantially photo-derived, so partial is supported; the traces are valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failures. rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The requested readout is not semantically sound. It treats one support failure as evidence that the corresponding requested feature is absent, and both failures as proof of no progress. But n1 and n2 only assess visible evidence under their criteria; a failure may not establish that the image has not been transformed in the requested way. The readout therefore overstates negative evidence and can return absent or partial without sufficient support. It also requires both supports to pass for completion, although their criteria do not establish that the whole image was converted into a chalk drawing. The program needs evidence that supports the requested extent, not merely chalk-like treatment and drawing form in isolation.

The requested readout is nested under n2, so it is activated only when n2 returns pass, fail, or unknown—which covers all allowed support statuses. However, its composition rules are contradictory: partial requires at least one support to pass, while unknown applies when no support passes and at least one is unknown; these conditions overlap when one support is unknown and the other fails. The program therefore does not define a unique readout for that evidence combination.

The support checks do not establish the requested extent reliably. n1 treats broad coverage of the main depicted content as evidence of progress but does not determine whether the whole image has been converted; n2 likewise allows a pass for drawing treatment across depicted content without defining or checking substantial unconverted areas consistently. The readout then permits complete when both supports pass and their evidence establishes broad treatment, so it can infer full-image conversion from coarse coverage. This fails the requirement that a coarse support pass not imply an unexamined finer condition.

The support checks cover chalk-like treatment and drawing form, but neither establishes whether the conversion applies to the image as a whole. The requested readout requires both supports to pass and their evidence to explicitly establish whole-image conversion, yet the supports do not collect that extent evidence. This leaves complete fulfillment unprovable even when both pass, so the program does not preserve the requested property and extent.

The requested readout requires evidence that the image as a whole was converted into a chalk drawing, but neither support check assesses whole-image coverage or remaining photographic areas. The readout cannot establish those facts from the saved observations, so its complete/partial criteria are unsupported. In addition, n3 treats both supports failing as absence, although failure only establishes that each specific cue was not established; the criteria themselves acknowledge that this does not prove no requested progress. The program therefore risks converting missing evidence into a negative result.
